concerns.text: Imputing missing metabolite‑class columns with zeros conflates true biological absence with missing data, violating construct validity of the metabolite abundance predictor.

Z‑score standardization across all species removes absolute concentration information, which may be essential for interpreting metabolite effects; this threatens construct validity of the predictor variables.

No formal power analysis is provided; with a minimum of 50 species (and reduced effective sample size after phylogenetic adjustment) the study may be under‑powered to detect modest effect sizes after multiple‑comparison correction.
Family is used only for stratified train/test split; it is not included as a covariate or random effect, leaving potential confounding by taxonomic relatedness unaddressed.

The plan does not specify how species IDs will be matched to the Open Tree of Life phylogeny, how missing taxa will be handled, or what statistical test will assess whether PGLS coefficients differ meaningfully from OLS (the >20 % change rule is arbitrary).

Permutation feature‑importance p‑values are mentioned but the permutation scheme, number of permutations, and justification for applying Benjamini‑Hochberg correction to importance scores are absent, making the inference method unsound.
